page: Microsoft Azure L4as_v4 is a virtual machine instance belonging to the Lasv4 family, powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz. It features 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with multithreading enabled, supported by 32.0 GB of system memory, which yields an 8.0 GB per core ratio. The instance includes 960 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, operating under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor on the x86_64 architecture.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Single-threaded tasks such as bzip3 decompression and Geekbench text processing also demonstrate strong results. However, multi-core scaling is moderate, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores falling into the average range. Memory bandwidth presents a notable bottleneck, with both small-block and large-block read-only memory bandwidth testing in the bottom 25%.

The L4as_v4 exhibits weak performance in database operations and software compilation, as evidenced by Passmark database and Clang compilation benchmarks. Large-model LLM inference is also a limitation, with medium-model prompt processing scoring in the bottom 10%. Given the 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and the bundled 960 GB local storage, this instance is configured for memory-intensive tasks, basic web serving, and single-threaded data processing workloads that do not require high multi-threaded memory throughput.

Performance benchmarks reveal strong single-core capabilities, highlighted by top-tier Geekbench single-core and single-threaded bzip3 decompression results. Conversely, multi-core scaling and memory read bandwidth are weaker, with database operations and software compilation benchmarks scoring in the bottom 25%. The 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes this instance suitable for memory-optimized workloads, text processing, and moderate web serving, though it is constrained in memory-intensive multi-threaded operations and large-scale database tasks.
